prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: It depends on your trip. Hotels are best if you want convenience, consistent service, and easy access to shows/Strip amenities. Airbnbs (especially cabins and lakefront houses) are best if you want space, a kitchen, or a quieter/lake-centered stay. Tell me your budget, group size, and priorities and I’ll recommend the single best pick — but here are quick guidelines and top choices by travel style.

Quick pros/cons
- Hotel: predictable service, daily housekeeping, front desk, pools, breakfast, shuttle/concierge help with shows. Best for short stays, show-goers, families who want low fuss.
- Airbnb/cabin: more space, full kitchen, better for groups/families wanting to cook or for longer stays; many gorgeous Table Rock Lake cabins. Quality and check-in vary; watch cleaning fees and cancellation rules.

Where to stay by traveler type (specific picks)
- Romantic/luxury, lake views:
  - Chateau on the Lake Resort Spa & Convention Center — lakefront, spa, upscale dining and views.
  - Big Cedar Lodge (near Branson) — high-end rustic resort with cabins, activities, and golf (great for a special trip).

- Best location for shows, dining, shopping (easy walking/short drives):
  - Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — right at Branson Landing waterfront shops and restaurants.
  - Hampton Inn & Suites Branson on the Strip (76 Country Blvd) — reliable, convenient to theaters and attractions.

- Family or groups who want resort amenities and kid-friendly fun:
  - Welk Resort Branson — condo-style units, pools, family activities.
  - Grand Country Inn & Waterpark / Grand Country Resort — good value, indoor water features and family packages.

- If you want a cabin or private home (Airbnb):
  - Search for “Table Rock Lake cabins” or “Indian Point cabins / Kimberling City / Hollister” for lakefront options and private docks.
  - Look for whole-house listings with lots of recent 5-star reviews, clear cancellation policy, and explicit sleeping arrangements for your group size.

Booking tips (to pick the right place)
- Map the property relative to the Strip, Branson Landing, Silver Dollar City, or Table Rock Lake depending on your priority.
- For shows: being on/near 76 Country Blvd saves driving; many hotels offer show shuttles or easy parking.
- For lake time: cabins/Big Cedar/Chateau give quicker access to the water.
- Check total price (cleaning, service, resort fees) not just the nightly rate.
- Read recent reviews for cleanliness, host responsiveness, and accurate listing photos.
- If traveling with kids, look for indoor pools/waterparks and kitchen facilities.
- If you need late check-in or show-friendly schedules, confirm front desk hours or self-check-in options.

If you tell me: dates, number of travelers, whether you want lake access or to be on the Strip, and approximate budget, I’ll give 2–3 best, tailored options (hotel vs Airbnb) with direct reasons.
